body:
# Architecture reference programme — design/review only

**Owner directive (2026-11-09):** Take architectural and product-quality ideas from the following EIGHT mature public projects and commercial products, **do not copy their code/UI/brand**, and adapt/extend the ideas to OpsControl's own roadmap, operating model, security, ETL execution evidence, Windows/Linux monitoring, and multi-customer tenancy.

Official references:
1. [OpenTelemetry organization](https://github.com/open-telemetry) and [Collector architecture](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/architecture/)
2. [SigNoz repository](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz) and [architecture](https://signoz.io/docs/architecture/)
3. [Uptime Kuma repository](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma)
4. [Prometheus repository](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus) and [architecture](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/)
5. [Grafana repository](https://github.com/grafana/grafana) and [dashboard documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/dashboards/) — dashboard design and interaction reference
6. [Sumo Logic](https://www.sumologic.com/) — [official documentation](https://www.sumologic.com/help/) for log analytics, parsers, monitored-source hierarchy and event investigation
7. [Datadog](https://www.datadoghq.com/) — [infrastructure documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/infrastructure/) for detailed host/process views, contextual tags, monitor rules and notification routing
8. [New Relic](https://newrelic.com/) — [entity and service-map documentation](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/new-relic-solutions/new-relic-one/core-concepts/what-entity-new-relic/) for entity-centric observability, correlation, dashboards and issue workflows

## Design-reference evaluation matrix

| Reference | Principle to study | OpsControl-specific improvement | Must not infer / copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenTelemetry | Receiver/processor/exporter/connector lifecycle, versioned config validation, signals | Template→source typed applicability, Windows/Linux processes/services, native ETL evidence adapters, source-generation/fencing, tenant routing | Do not claim OTel SDK/Collector itself solves exactly-once or CHK-001 persistent queue loss; keep 0.123.0 pin |
| SigNoz | Correlated metrics/logs/traces, contextual drill-down, custom views, dependency maps, progressive UX | Resource→process→ETL execution→evidence→incident chain with verified/unverified states and one tenant scope | No default ClickHouse migration, no copying dashboards or claims of implemented features |
| Uptime Kuma | Onboarding simplicity, status cards, responsive UX, history, notifications, accessible self-hosted installation | Enterprise-safe resource setup wizard, status freshness/unknown distinction, scoped customer views and audit, operator-focused compact layout | No route or backend simplification that bypasses RBAC/tenant isolation; no invented live checks |
| Prometheus | Labels/time-series, histograms, range queries, rule evaluation/validation, recording rules, Alertmanager-style dedup/routing | Time range/frequency controls; host/process/API thresholds with cardinality budgets; keep deterministic execution/attempt/event ledger as source of truth for ETL | No use of scrape samples as proof that a job started/finished, no unbounded label cardinality; no default new TSDB |
| **Grafana — dashboard design** | Panel organization, consistent variables and filters, time-range controls, drill-down links, dashboard layouts, annotations, thresholds and accessible data visualization | OpsControl overview, resource/host/process detail, ETL execution timeline, APIs, historical metrics, customer-scoped dashboard filters and freshness/unknown visual states | No copying Grafana UI/code/branding/assets, no unapproved Grafana dependency or datasource architecture replacement; do not suggest implemented or healthy telemetry without evidence |

| **Sumo Logic — log and event investigation** | Structured log search, source taxonomy, field extraction/normalization, pivot from event to monitored entity, prioritized signal investigation | Host/process/ETL log search with immutable provenance, bounded tenant-checked filters, event→metric→execution drill-down and explicit evidence confidence | Do not copy proprietary SIEM rules, queries, connectors or code; no unapproved SIEM product expansion or unverified correlation |
| **Datadog — host/process and alert UX** | Host/process explorer, tag grouping, live and historical metrics, scoped monitor rules and notification deduplication | Selected Windows/Linux processes/services, resource consumption trends, host→process drill-down, customer/environment filters and noise-resistant routing | No copied product UI/agent/code, no secret-bearing command-line exposure, unbounded cardinality or unproven sampling claims |
| **New Relic — entity-centric relationships** | Entity catalogue, service/dependency relationships, time-scoped queries, alert issue grouping and routed workflows | Customer→resource→process/service→ETL execution→evidence lineage, historical context and verified relationship confidence | No copying proprietary NRQL, UI or service maps; no automatic cross-customer relationship inference or New Relic service dependency |

## OpsControl differentiated product contract

Focus: **evidence-based operations control plane** for self-hosted customer-isolated Windows/Linux VM/process/service health, APIs and ETL pipelines. In one view, show real-time/latest samples, historical range, source + collector freshness, causal/identity evidence, expected schedule vs actual execution, alert/incident status, ownership and audited configuration revision.

Principles:
- OTel-compatible telemetry transports, native execution evidence & authoritative separate PostgreSQL records; preserve existing React/Vite + FastAPI + SQLAlchemy/Alembic + PostgreSQL and agreed centralized PostgreSQL durable-spool architecture design.
- Customer identity and internal department authorization remain different; enforce server-side tenant access, no cross-tenant leakage.
- Distinguish UNKNOWN/UNVERIFIED/STALE/NO_RUN/FAILED/HEALTHY; never display synthetic monitored health.
- Preserve controlled collection (no ETL job execution/repair/cancel), immutable evidence and revisions, source fencing and idempotency.
- Alerts: prevention of false-positive flapping via consecutive conditions, debounce/hysteresis, grouping/correlation, actionable evidence and deduped notifications; coordinate with existing alert and notification engine rather than rewrite.
- Future metric/history experiences: configurable time range, aggregation/frequency, relevant CPU/memory/disk/network and selected Windows/Linux processes/services, accessible dense tables and comparison, retention/series cardinality and data-freshness controls.
- Reference design **does not** authorize architecture changes, new storage engines, collector upgrades, migrations, code copying, license clearance, completion/certification statements, deployments or merges.

## Proposed staged discovery (not an implementation order approval)

**A.** Reference-to-requirement gap map: classify implemented, partial, blocked, planned, or rejected. Cite exact OpsControl modules and actual tests. Benchmark query performance, ingestion reliability, card density, accessibility, setup flow and operational semantics. Avoid feature creep.

**B.** Architecture RFCs only where useful: signal schema/labels/cardinality; source/collector lifecycle; process discovery and selection; metric retention and query; alert rule DSL and notification delivery; ETL evidence/attempt/provenance; multi-tenant security and durability. Each RFC identifies owner decision and trade-offs, compatibility/migration and independent acceptance tests.

**C.** Product UX prototypes: Grafana-inspired (not copied) configurable dashboard panels, resource & process explorer, ETL execution timeline, cross-signal investigation, shared time-range/aggregation controls, drill-downs, annotations and easy onboarding. Maintain owner-approved Resource Management visual baseline; product typography Issue #90 separate.

**D.** Architecture, performance, security and release gates: isolate PostgreSQL, CI positive/negative tests, crash/replay, RBAC/tenant, browser, source credentials and lifecycle. Preserve CHK-001 FAIL, CHK-002 BLOCKED, SECURITY BLOCKED, RELEASE NO-GO, 13 ruleset checks; no automatic release or feature-status promotion.

## Workstream boundary

Codex is already performing OC-S1-CI-004 on draft #89. **Do not touch #89**, run parallel implementation, or silently modify core architecture. This issue captures reference research and roadmap design decisions, pending owner prioritization after existing acceptance gates.


## Owner direction approval — 2026-11-09 (roadmap level)

**APPROVED:** Use all five references (OpenTelemetry, SigNoz, Uptime Kuma, Prometheus and Grafana) as a research/design/architecture improvement framework for OpsControl. Develop original implementations and preserve independent product identity; do **not** copy code, UI designs, illustrations, branding or presume license compatibility. This approval covers the reference strategy and development-phase objective, not unreviewed technology replacements, migrations, collector pins or production deployment.

**Development definition of complete:** implement **and verify** each end-to-end workflow supported by the project, or explicitly mark it BLOCKED/PARTIAL if real-provider certification, durability or external dependency is not available. Maintain distinctions between (1) implemented code, (2) controlled integration evidence, (3) genuine-provider/runtime qualification, (4) security/reliability acceptance, and (5) release approval. Mock demos/static screenshots are not certifications.

**Timing:** Sprint 1 PR #89 remains the active closure priority, with Codex independently working on its authorized task. After Sprint 1, conduct separate owner decisions for the typography family/scale (Issue #90), product name/logo/market identity (Issue #93), reference-derived architecture and feature prioritization (this issue), and final Apache-2.0 licensing/legal clearance (Issue #91). The owner has **not** chosen a specific font, logo, brand name, storage replacement, version upgrade or license activation merely by approving the programme.

The end-to-end acceptance and certification inventory is tracked separately as **OC-E2E-001, Issue #94**. No merge, deployment, production security waiver or Sprint 2 execution authorization is implied. CHK-001 FAIL, CHK-002 BLOCKED, SECURITY BLOCKED and RELEASE NO-GO remain in force.


## Owner approval and Sprint 1 boundary — 2026-11-09

**APPROVED as product-reference and architecture direction:** All eight reference products (OpenTelemetry, SigNoz, Uptime Kuma, Prometheus and Grafana) are approved for **ideas, comparative engineering standards, and original OpsControl improvements**. The goal in the **development phase** is to **implement OR provide honest, reproducible certification evidence for each approved end-to-end workflow**; feature code alone, synthetic fixture PASS, screenshots, or architecture sign-off do not count as full runtime/provider certification.

**Defer individual decisions until after Sprint 1:** font family/scale (#90), final brand name/logo/trademark clearance (#93), detailed architecture RFCs or changed storage/collector design, GitHub showcase rollout, and final Apache-2.0 packaging/legal signoff (#91). Approval of reference principles is **not** an approval of every specific mechanism; record individual design/implementation choices and required evidence separately.

**Approved small Sprint 1 architecture alignment patch:** tracked in [OC-S1-ARCH-001](https://github.com/Parikshit-Sahrawat/OpsControl_Dashboard/issues/95). Scope must be bounded to existing architecture documentation, cross-signal source-of-truth and state declarations, and an exact-test/evidence E2E workflow matrix. Existing real CI/functional regression coverage may be improved without relaxing gates. No new telemetry backend, Grafana embedding, database redesign, unapproved agent upgrades, metric or incidents UI expansion, or copied third-party code. The patch is sequenced **after** current Codex work on draft PR #89 to avoid competing branch writes; no current CI/security remediation should be interrupted.

**Sprint 1 acceptance remains distinct:** owner visual approval already recorded; independent engineering review, GitHub required checks, image security/licence review and provider/operational evidence remain separate gates. CHK-001 FAIL · CHK-002 BLOCKED · SECURITY BLOCKED · RELEASE NO-GO.

## Additional owner-approved reference inputs — 2026-11-09

The owner has explicitly added **Sumo Logic, Datadog and New Relic** under the same *reference-and-improve, never copy* rule. Their public concepts are evaluated through official product documentation and original OpsControl design decisions, not through code/asset transplantation. These are **benchmarking references**, not approved dependencies, SIEM/AI feature commitments, licensed reuse, or runtime certification.

Priority applications for later individual approvals:
- Sumo Logic: log search and normalization, evidence pivots, event relationship confidence and filtered investigations.
- Datadog: selected Windows/Linux process monitoring, tag/facet filters, host inventory, effective threshold/dedup/notification routing.
- New Relic: explicit resource/process/ETL execution entity relationships, historical context, controlled issue/alert correlation.

For the **small Sprint 1 patch #95**, include traceability rows for these references in the architecture notes; **do not expand implementation** beyond the previously approved bounded architecture alignment and E2E evidence matrix. Individual feature, storage, agent, licensing and UX decisions remain AFTER Sprint 1. Preserve excluded Kubernetes distributions and existing CI/security/durability gates.
